jess: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change in canary we're seeing ~30% CPU increase on the host-side tokenization path and a spike in small gRPC write syscalls. Repro on staging with loadtest 1k qps. logs attached below. :eyes:
jess: Example pprof snapshot (top):
``n(pprof) top10
0.38s  12.3%  token::split (host_preparse.cc:142)
0.26s   8.4%  grpc::Writev (grpc_stream.cc:87)
0.21s   6.8%  kernel_selector::choose_best (kernel_picker.cc:213)
0.19s   6.2%  kvcache::lookup (kv_cache.cc:58)
```
sam: Ack — pinging rui and maria. Do we have flamegraphs or a syscall trace? Is the regression correlated with sequence length distribution change or just the kernel pick? :thinking:
rui: I pushed a flamegraph to the staging artifacts: https://staging-artifacts/internal/fg/6077777777.svg — main hotspot is token::split inner loop, but stack shows kernel_selector called right before the slow path. Looks like the selector picks a kernel that favors memory coalescing but forces extra copies in host preparse.
maria: Observed kvcache miss-rate jumped from 2% -> 7% during the canary window. That could explain more tokenization work if prefixes aren't cached and we reparse. Also grpc small writes up ~40% (many 1-3 writev calls per request).
ken: Quick mitigation: change batching_heuristics.min_batch to 4 and enable small_write_coalesce=true in runtime-config; should reduce writev count and amortize tokenization over a slightly larger batch. Can try a canary patch.
jess: I'll try ken's config on one canary host. If we still see the CPU, we should rollback the kernel_selector commit.
sam: Can someone paste the exact git hash for the kernel-selector change? Need for revert if needed.
maria: Hash is a1b2c3d4 (PR #1892). Also adding a metric: host_tokenization_cpu and grpc_writev_ops to staging dashboards.
deploy-bot: Deploy started for runtime-config change by ken on svc/host-preparse-canary (canary=1/5).
jess: After the config canary (10m) — CPU dropped ~12%, writev ops down ~25%. Still above baseline but much improved. Collecting another pprof. :thumbsup:
rui: If the config helps, follow-up plan: tweak kernel-selector to prefer kernels without extra host-side copies when preparse path is active. I can prototype a heuristic: if kvcache.miss_rate > 5% prefer kernel_fast_no_copy.
ken: I'll open a small PR to gate selector with that heuristic and add unit tests.
jess: Great. Let's keep the canary running for 1 hour and regroup. Thanks all.
